result.topic_en: The page reduces the integral to Euler's canonical biquadratic relation and identifies its coefficients. Corollary III then sets A = 0 and substitutes xx, yy for x, y to integrate the differential equation with sixth-degree polynomials under the radicals. It closes by announcing that the same integral will be obtained by Lagrange's method.
result.transcription:
quae porro reducta et per $(x-y)^2$ diuisa reuocatur ad hanc formam:
$\frac{2A \mp 2\sqrt{AK}}{kk} = \frac{A(x+y)^2}{kkxy} - Exy - \frac{A}{xy}$
siue ad hanc:
$\frac{A}{kk}(xx+yy-kk) - Exxyy \pm \frac{2xy\sqrt{AK}}{kk} = 0$
quae egregie conuenit cum aequatione canonica, qua olim sum vsus: scil.
$0 = \alpha + \gamma(xx+yy) + 2\delta xy + \zeta xxyy$
si quidem est
$\alpha = -\frac{A}{kk}; \gamma = +\frac{A}{kk}; 2\delta = \pm\frac{2\sqrt{AK}}{kk}; \zeta = -E$
Corollarium III.
§. 72. Methodo posteriore, qua hic vsi sumus ad hanc aequationem integrandam, aequatio multo generalior tractari poterit, vbi in formulis radicalibus potestates vsque ad sextam dimensionem assurgunt. Namque si tantum statuamus $A=0$, vt sit aequatio
$\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x(B+Cx+Dxx+Ex^3)}} \pm \frac{dy}{\sqrt{y(B+Cy+Dyy+Ey^3)}} = 0$
eius integrale est
$\frac{B(x+y)+2Cxy+Dxy(x+y)+2Exxyy}{(x-y)^2}$
$\mp\frac{2\sqrt{xy(B+Cx+Dxx+Ex^3)(B+Cy+Dyy+Ay^3)}}{(x-y)^2} = \frac{B}{k}$ [?]
Quod si iam hic loco $x$ et $y$ scribamus $xx$ et $yy$, aequatio differentialis fiet
$\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(B+Cxx+Dx^4+Ex^6)}} \pm \frac{dy}{\sqrt{(B+Cyy+Dy^4+Ey^6)}} = 0,$
cuius ergo integrale erit
$\frac{B(xx+yy)+2Cxxyy+Dxxyy(xx+yy)+2Ex^4y^4}{(xx-yy)^2}$
$\mp\frac{2xy\sqrt{(B+Cxx+Dx^4+Ex^6)(B+Cyy+Dy^4+Ey^6)}}{(xx-yy)^2} = \frac{B}{kk}.$
Nunc autem ostendamus, quomodo ope methodi Illustris de la Grange idem integrale impetrari queat.

items.quote: Methodo posteriore, qua hic vsi sumus ad hanc aequationem integrandam, aequatio multo generalior tractari poterit, vbi in formulis radicalibus potestates vsque ad sextam dimensionem assurgunt.
items.english: By the latter method, which we used here to integrate this equation, a much more general equation can be treated, in which the powers in the radical formulas rise up to the sixth degree.

items.quote: Nunc autem ostendamus, quomodo ope methodi Illustris de la Grange idem integrale impetrari queat.
items.english: Now let us show how, by means of the method of the illustrious de la Grange, the same integral can be obtained.
